text: The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on Group, Organization, and Project records, gated by a hierarchy-management capability.
The system shall allow an Organization to optionally belong to a Group; an Organization not assigned to a Group shall operate as fully independent.
Deleting a Group shall not delete its member Organizations; deleting an Organization shall cascade-delete its Projects and directly-scoped user accounts and AI activation/override state.

The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on Organizational Breakdown Structure (OBS) entries, each typed or free-text, optionally parented to another OBS entry, forming a per-Organization or per-Project tree.
The system shall prevent deleting an OBS node from breaking referential integrity, either by cascading or by re-parenting/reassigning dependent records.
The system shall display, for every OBS node, a live count of linked item types, so accountability and activity concentration are visible at a glance.
The system shall enforce the active Solution Pack's maximum-Projects and maximum-OBS-node quotas at creation time, server-side, rejecting an over-quota request with HTTP 409.
The system shall ensure that no Organization can enumerate, query, or infer the existence of another Organization through any API response, error message, or shared identifier sequence.

The system shall display, on every Organization list and detail screen, whether the Organization belongs to a Group (Yes/No) and, if so, which Group; an Organization with no Group shall be labeled Independent.

The system shall reject, server-side, an OBS parent assignment that crosses trees — an Organization-level node under a Project-level node, or a node under another Project's tree — and an assignment that makes a node its own ancestor.

The system shall identify records by values that reveal nothing about other tenants' activity — opaque identifiers (e.g. UUIDs) or per-tenant sequences — and shall answer a request for another tenant's record exactly as for a record that does not exist (HTTP 404), in support of FR-DA-TEN-08.

The system shall present a tenancy tree, Group (Yes/No) > Organization > principal records, and the same content as a table (Group Yes/No, Group, Organization, sector, records), limited to the Organizations the viewer may see.

The system shall let an authorized user choose the Organization a new principal record belongs to before creating it, showing whether that Organization belongs to a Group; a platform administrator may choose any Organization, other users only their own.

The system shall provision every new Organization on creation with the OBS skeleton, the standard governance catalog, the AI Use Case Library (FR-DA-AI-02), the checklist and record templates, and, when requested, a starting team of one account per standard role under the Organization's e-mail domain with an initial password; a domain already used by another Organization shall be refused.

The system shall let a dedicated permission grant read-only visibility of the principal records of the other Organizations of the viewer's own Group; records of Organizations outside the Group shall never be visible, and records of another Organization shall never be editable from the viewer's Organization.

The system shall let an OBS node list the people placed in it, each with a standard role and the role played in that node (for example "Engineering lead" in a project team), and shall let an administrator add and remove them.
The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on user accounts, including name, email/username, one or more assigned roles, and language preference.

The system shall provide a Permission Matrix screen displaying every permission/capability code against every role, editable by users holding a dedicated permission-management capability, with edits taking effect immediately and platform-wide without a code change.

The system shall enforce every API endpoint, server-side, against the authenticated user's resolved permission set (the union across all assigned roles); a request lacking the required permission shall be rejected with HTTP 403.
The system shall enforce that the Owner and the Evaluator of any two-party verification step are never the same user, both in the UI and at the server.
The system shall provide a minimal user directory (id, name, email) accessible to any authenticated user for assignment purposes, independent of the full user-management permission.

The system shall issue a signed, time-boxed authentication token on successful login, required on every subsequent API call, and shall never expose a stored password hash or credential via any API response.
The system shall expose a single platform-wide justification-required toggle (Section 3.7), defaulting to on, gated by a hierarchy/governance-management capability.

The system shall, when a user opens a screen or deep link that their roles or the Organization's configuration do not allow, show an in-app access notice explaining why and whom to ask, never a blank page or a raw error.

The system shall provide a dedicated permission for viewing the content of individual evaluation or verification verdicts; other users, except the parties to that verification, shall see that an evaluation exists but not its content.

The system shall, at startup, add any permission code introduced by a new release to the catalog together with its default role grants, without overwriting grants an administrator has changed (Section 3.13).

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall record, per Organization, exactly one Solution Pack as the single source of truth for that Organization's feature and quota entitlements, defined centrally in one configuration module and consumed by every enforcing route, so entitlements are never duplicated or able to drift between routes.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall define, for each Solution Pack, at minimum: which modules/features are enabled, the AI tier available (Assistive-only vs. Assistive+Augmented), and numeric ceilings on Projects, OBS nodes, and AI Use Cases.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall record a set of priced Add-Ons, each an independent toggle that grants its associated feature to a Pack that does not already include it standard.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall record a set of priced Compliance & Security Standards modules (at minimum GDPR, ISO/IEC 27001, and SOC 2), each an independent toggle available regardless of Solution Pack.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall, on activating a Compliance & Security Standard, idempotently seed a starting Controls scaffold tagged to that framework, without duplicating it on repeated activation, and shall not delete any Control tagged to a Standard that is later deactivated.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall enforce every Pack-gated feature and every Add-On/Compliance-gated feature server-side via dedicated middleware on the corresponding API route, independently of and in addition to RBAC permission checks; a request for a feature the active configuration does not include shall be rejected with HTTP 403, naming the missing feature.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall expose the Organization's effective configuration and the static Pack/Add-On/Compliance catalog to every authenticated user regardless of role, so client-side navigation can correctly show or hide gated menu items; this read is a UX convenience, not the enforcement boundary.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall expose current usage against every quota dimension, computed live from current data, and shall visually flag a quota that meets or exceeds its allotment.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall never represent, in any UI text, Help content, FAQ answer, or generated document, that activating a Compliance & Security Standard constitutes a certification, an external audit, or a legal attestation of compliance.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall allow an authorized Organization administrator to register, configure, enable, and disable a connection to an external application through the External Integration Registry (Section 3.3), independently of any other registered integration.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall store every external integration's credentials using the same client-side-only or encrypted-server-side pattern already required for the Real LLM Provider Connection (NFR-DA-SEC-07), never in plaintext, and never logged.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall verify an external integration's connection health on demand and shall record the outcome (success, authentication failure, unreachable) with a timestamp, without exposing provider-side error detail that could aid an unrelated attacker.

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall allow an authorized administrator to map fields between an external application's records and the platform's own entities, and shall log every inbound or outbound integration transaction (record, timestamp, direction, and result) for audit (Section 4.11).

section: 4.3 Configuration Management (Solution Packs, Add-Ons, Compliance Standards)
text: The system shall accept inbound events from an external application only through the Multi-Channel Communication webhook channel (Section 4.17) or an equivalent authenticated endpoint, never an unauthenticated route, and shall scope every inbound event to the Organization that registered the originating integration.

The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, Delete, and version-revert on an AI Use Case catalog, each entry capturing an id, name, tier (Assistive/Augmented), owning module, trigger, expected output, a human-checkpoint description, and versioned prompt-template content, gated by a dedicated AI-use-case-management capability.

The system shall seed every Organization with the same library of AI Use Cases on creation, and shall allow an Organization to additionally author custom AI Use Cases up to its active Solution Pack's custom-use-case quota.

The system shall create Version 1 of an AI Use Case automatically on creation, mark it Default/Current, and shall retain the full version history indefinitely; reverting to a historical version shall duplicate its content into a brand-new Current version, never rewrite or delete history.

The system shall allow an Organization Administrator to activate or deactivate any AI Use Case for the whole Organization, and shall allow an authorized Project-level user to set a tri-state (Inherit/On/Off) override per Project; effective activation shall resolve the Project override when set, else the Organization's activation state.

The system shall block, server-side, any new AI suggestion from a deactivated AI Use Case (by its effective state) immediately on deactivation, while never retroactively hiding or removing content a human already reviewed and approved before deactivation.

The system shall visually label every AI-generated output, wherever shown, as AI-generated and requiring human review, alongside its tier and its generation source (deterministic built-in engine or a configured live model).

The system shall write an append-only AI Usage Log entry for every AI suggestion's outcome (Accepted, Edited, or Rejected), capturing the use case, Organization, Project, the record it applied to, the acting user, and a timestamp; the log shall expose no edit or delete route.

The system shall allow a user to configure a Real LLM Provider Connection (provider, model, endpoint, API key) that is persisted client-side only, is forwarded once per generation request, is never returned in any API response, never written to any log, never cached or persisted server-side beyond that single request, and is never included in any data export.

The system shall, on any failure of a live LLM call, fall back automatically to the AI Use Case's deterministic built-in generator, so a misconfigured or unreachable connection never blocks a suggestion from being produced.
The system shall ensure an AI Use Case's activation, tier, or generation never grants a user visibility into data beyond what their RBAC role and permissions already allow.

The system shall, before generating any suggestion, ground it in retrieved reference content (Section 4.5), instruct the underlying model to stay within the application's own vocabulary, and state no number, score, or name not present in the retrieved references or the record's own data; the retrieved references shall be disclosed to the user alongside the output.

The system shall show every active AI Use Case, labelled with its tier (Assistive AI or Augmented AI) by a distinct icon and wording, on the processes, macro processes, tasks and steps it is linked to, and shall let an authorized user run it there and accept, modify or reject the suggestion (FR-DA-AI-07).

The system shall let an AI Use Case be linked to a step, a process, a task or an end-to-end process, and shall list the tasks of the process design with the AI Use Cases that support them, filterable by tier.
The system shall let an authorized user delete a custom AI Use Case, keeping its usage-log entries; seeded catalog entries shall be deactivated instead of deleted.

The system shall offer, wherever the live model is configured (personal settings and administration), a provider list and a model list with a "custom model" choice and an optional custom endpoint, and a connection test that reports only the outcome category (works, authentication failure, model not found, rate limited, unreachable).

The system shall maintain a Standards/Knowledge Base of reference content — regulatory or methodological standards, or per-process/per-stage practitioner guidance — available in every language the platform supports.

The system shall index this knowledge base, the tenant's own historical records, and a static application-feature/FAQ corpus using the same retrieval mechanism, so AI Use Case grounding, an AI Assistant's application-help mode, and any chatbot share one retrieval engine rather than several.
The system shall scope every retrieval query to the requesting user's own tenant; no cross-tenant record shall appear in a retrieval result or an AI suggestion.

The system shall gracefully degrade when a live LLM call is unavailable or fails: the retrieval result (the matched reference content, the computed fact) shall still be returned, rather than the request failing outright.

section: 4.6 Process/Stage Governance (Alerts, Business Rules, Controls, Risks, RACSI, Custom KPIs)
text: The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on Business Rules, each with a condition, an action, a severity, and an owner, gated by a governance-management capability and, where the platform separates GRC from the base module set, by the active Solution Pack's GRC entitlement.

section: 4.6 Process/Stage Governance (Alerts, Business Rules, Controls, Risks, RACSI, Custom KPIs)
text: The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on Controls, each classified under one of the five COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework components, with a control type, testing frequency, owner, and effectiveness rating.

section: 4.6 Process/Stage Governance (Alerts, Business Rules, Controls, Risks, RACSI, Custom KPIs)
text: The system shall allow a Control to be optionally tagged with the Compliance & Security Standard it was seeded under or otherwise supports, without that tag itself constituting a certification (Section 4.3, FR-DA-CFG-09).

section: 4.6 Process/Stage Governance (Alerts, Business Rules, Controls, Risks, RACSI, Custom KPIs)
text: The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on Risk/Opportunity items, each with a type, a likelihood (1–5) and impact (1–5) rating, an automatically computed score, an owner, and a status, and shall render a 5×5 likelihood × impact heat-map.

section: 4.6 Process/Stage Governance (Alerts, Business Rules, Controls, Risks, RACSI, Custom KPIs)
text: The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on Custom KPIs, additive to the platform's built-in KPI set, each with a plain-language formula description, a target, and an owner, available regardless of Solution Pack.

section: 4.6 Process/Stage Governance (Alerts, Business Rules, Controls, Risks, RACSI, Custom KPIs)
text: The system shall support a RACSI accountability matrix: full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on RACSI Activities, each optionally linked to a process step or to a specific Business Rule, Control, or Risk/Opportunity record, and on RACSI Assignments, each assigning exactly one of the five RACSI roles to a named person or a role.

section: 4.6 Process/Stage Governance (Alerts, Business Rules, Controls, Risks, RACSI, Custom KPIs)
text: The system shall enforce that a RACSI Activity has at most one Accountable assignment at any time, both in the UI and at the data-persistence layer.

section: 4.6 Process/Stage Governance (Alerts, Business Rules, Controls, Risks, RACSI, Custom KPIs)
text: The system shall allow a Business Rule, a Control, a Risk/Opportunity, and a RACSI Activity to each be optionally tagged with the owning OBS node and with the process/stage they are most relevant to, and shall surface the items tagged to a given process/stage on that process/stage's own governance view.

The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on BPMN Diagrams, each with a title, description, and a BPMN 2.0-compliant XML payload, rendered/edited with a standards-compliant BPMN 2.0 modeler/viewer component, not a static image.

The system shall grant read-only pan/zoom viewing of a BPMN Diagram to any user holding view access, and shall grant the full editing palette and a Save action only to users holding edit access whose Organization's active configuration includes full BPMN editing.
The system shall render the BPMN editor's tool palette in a dedicated panel beside the diagram canvas, structurally separate from the canvas, rather than floating over it.

The system shall provide Export (download the current diagram as a schema-valid .bpmn/XML file) and Import (load a .bpmn/XML file, replacing the current diagram) actions, so a diagram is portable to and from any other BPMN 2.0-compliant tool.
The system shall be seeded, per Organization, with at least one BPMN Diagram modeling the application's own core process end-to-end.

The system shall offer a shapes palette section grouped by category (tools, events, activities, gateways, data, participants, artifacts), usable by click or drag, and shown as a legend of the main shapes when the diagram is view-only.

The system shall let the user open a diagram in a full-screen workspace with the palette, zoom controls (slider, zoom in and out, fit), a palette that slides away, and a single action or the Escape key to return to the page.

The system shall state on the diagram screen whether editing a diagram changes the execution of records; where diagrams only document the process, saving one shall not alter running or future records.
The system shall compute the platform's standard KPIs in real time from current data, scoped to the requesting user's tenant.

The system shall provide a set of standard reports, each exportable on demand as a downloadable PDF, Excel (.xlsx), and Word (.docx) file, generated server-side and styled to the suite's common visual identity.
The system shall name every exported report file with the report key and the export date, and shall serve it with the correct MIME type and a Content-Disposition attachment header.

The system shall offer a client-side CSV export on its highest-traffic tables, reflecting exactly the rows and columns currently on screen and respecting the same RBAC and scope filtering as the table itself, written with a UTF-8 byte-order mark so accented and Arabic content opens correctly in common spreadsheet tools.

The system shall define a shared Alert Catalog naming every alert type once, with a human-readable name and a primary process/stage tag, consumed identically by seed data and by live computation, so alert semantics cannot drift between demo data and live behavior.
The system shall surface a persistent, dismissible per-tenant or per-project alert inbox, with a live unread-alert indicator in the primary navigation.
The system shall avoid raising a duplicate alert of the same type against the same triggering entity within the same period.
The system shall allow a user to mark an individual alert as read, and, where dismissal is supported, shall persist the dismissal separately from the alert's own (recomputed) state.

The system shall allow an authorized user to independently enable or disable each alert type, displaying its human-readable name alongside its machine code in both the alert inbox and any governance-settings configuration list.
The system shall provide a data-query mode that answers natural-language questions about the requesting user's own organization by matching the question to a fixed set of data-query intents.

The system shall associate every data-query intent with the single RBAC permission required to answer it, and shall evaluate that permission after matching the intent but strictly before running any query; when the permission is missing, the system shall return an explicit, human-readable refusal naming the missing permission rather than executing the query.
The system shall scope every data-query answer to the requesting user's own tenant, consistent with the platform's multi-tenancy requirement (Section 4.1).

The system shall provide an application-help mode answering “Can it…?” / “How do I…?” questions by ranking a static FAQ/feature corpus with the same retrieval engine used elsewhere in the platform (Section 4.5).
The system shall render the AI Assistant both as a dedicated screen and as a floating widget accessible from every authenticated screen, without navigating away from the user's current work.

The system shall gate the AI Assistant behind a single view permission and the active Solution Pack's AI Assistant entitlement, independent of and in addition to any module-specific permission a given data-query intent may separately require.
The system shall write an audit or change-log entry for every state-changing operation on a governed field, capturing the actor, timestamp, entity type/id, and the before/after value.

The system shall follow the stage-then-justify pattern (Section 3.7) for every score or state change to a governed record: staging a new value, requiring or offering a justification note per the platform-wide toggle, and appending both atomically to the record's audit/change log in one update.
The system shall make the audit/change log viewable, read-only, to users holding an audit-view permission, and shall never expose an edit or delete route for it.
The system shall ensure audit-log writes never block or fail the primary operation they accompany.

The system shall allow an authorized user to reopen a completed workflow step before the stage or approval it belongs to is decided, only with a justification recorded per Section 3.7; the reopening shall return the step to its active state and be written to the audit log.
The system shall provide an in-app Help screen presenting topic articles covering every module of the application, accessible to every authenticated user independent of role or permission grants.
The system shall render Help content in the user's currently selected display language, matching the article set one-to-one across every supported language.
The system shall provide a free-text search box on the Help screen filtering topics by a case-insensitive match against the topic title or body.

The system shall provide, next to every scored or classified input (for example complexity scores), a decision matrix describing each level, and shall show a legend for every code or colour vocabulary displayed in a list or matrix (for example the Part letter of a process or the status colours of a matrix).

The system shall support a library of pre-filled starting points (templates) for its principal record type, each capturing default field values a new record can be seeded from, while leaving every field editable before submission.

The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on templates, versioned via the same version-history mechanism as the AI Use Case Library (Section 4.4), gated by a dedicated template-management capability.
The system shall make templates available regardless of Solution Pack, consistent with the always-standard treatment of Custom KPIs and standard Reports.
Deleting a template shall not affect any record already created from it; a template is a starting point copied at use time, not a live-linked reference.
The system shall manage project templates through the Project Template Catalog of Section 4.33; the rules of FR-DA-TPL-01 to 04 apply to it.

The system shall provide complete UI translation in English, French, and Arabic for all navigation, labels, form fields, statuses, and messages, with no hardcoded UI string outside the shared translation dictionary.
The system shall allow a user to change their display language at any time without reloading or losing unsaved work.
The system shall persist a user's language preference and apply it automatically on subsequent logins, resolved per the precedence order in Section 3.6.
The system shall render the entire application right-to-left, including navigation, forms, tables, and charts, when Arabic is selected.
The system shall allow an Organization to configure a tenant-level default language.

The system shall allow adding a new supported language by configuration — populating the shared translation dictionary (Section 3.6) — alone, without a code change or a redeployment of application logic.

The system shall return every server-generated, user-facing message — validation and error messages, notification text, AI Assistant answers, and export labels — in the requesting user's display language, resolved from the same translation dictionary as the UI; a machine code may accompany the translated text but shall not replace it.

The system shall seed its reference and Knowledge Base content in every supported language and shall let the user filter Knowledge Base articles by language, defaulting to the user's display language.

The system shall allow any set of Actions the user selects to be grouped into a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), organized as a tree of WBS nodes, each node referencing one or more Action IDs as its leaf-level work items.

The system shall allow a WBS node or a referenced Action to carry a planned start date, planned end date or duration, percent-complete, and zero or more predecessor dependencies on other WBS nodes or Actions within the same WBS.

The system shall render a WBS as a Gantt chart, plotting every node and its referenced Actions on a shared timeline, drawing dependency lines between predecessor and successor items, and visually distinguishing planned, in-progress, completed, and overdue items.

The system shall recompute a WBS node’s own planned dates and percent-complete from its child nodes/Actions when the node itself is not directly scheduled, so a summary bar always reflects the current state of its children without manual reconciliation.

The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on WBS structures, and shall allow the same Action to be referenced from more than one WBS without duplicating the underlying Action record.
The system shall export a WBS/Gantt view to at least one portable format (e.g. PDF or an image), consistent with the platform’s standard Reports & Data Export conventions (Section 4.8).

The system shall provide a single, generic Version Management service (Section 3.8) that any governed entity type can register with, rather than each entity type implementing its own history mechanism.
The system shall create an initial version automatically when a versioned entity is created, mark it Current, and create a new version — never overwrite the prior one — on every subsequent edit.

The system shall retain every version of a versioned entity indefinitely, with no hard-delete route for a historical version, and shall allow an authorized user to view the full version history and compare any two versions field-by-field.

The system shall allow an authorized user to revert a versioned entity to any historical version; reverting shall duplicate that version’s content into a brand-new Current version, never rewrite or delete the entity’s history, consistent with the pattern already defined for the AI Use Case Library (FR-DA-AI-03) and Template Libraries (FR-DA-TPL-02).

The system shall record, on every version, the acting user, a timestamp, and — where the platform-wide justification toggle (Section 3.7) requires it — the justification note that accompanied the change.

The system shall provide one shared version-comparison view, available from the history of every versioned entity, that shows two selected versions side by side and highlights the fields that differ, in support of FR-DA-VER-03.

The system shall support delivering a notification or alert (Section 4.9) through one or more channels — at minimum in-app, email, and webhook, with SMS and push as optional channels — behind a single shared dispatch interface (Section 3.9).
The system shall allow a user to independently enable or disable each available channel for each notification category, defaulting every category to the in-app channel at minimum.
The system shall compose a message once, per notification event, and render it in the recipient’s own display language (Section 3.6) before dispatch to any channel.

The system shall record a delivery-status record per message per channel (queued, sent, delivered, failed), and shall retry a failed delivery on that channel’s own schedule without blocking or duplicating delivery on any other channel.

The system shall never send a tenant’s data through an external channel provider (email, SMS, push) beyond the minimum content required for that notification, and shall scope every dispatch to the recipient’s own tenant.

The system shall prompt for a REX entry when the application’s principal record reaches a terminal/closed status, and when an individual Action is marked complete, without blocking the closure itself on the REX entry being filled in.

The system shall structure every REX entry with, at minimum: what went well, what did not, a root-cause note, a recommendation/improvement action, a category/tag, and an effectiveness or satisfaction rating on a fixed scale.

The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on REX entries, each optionally tagged to the owning OBS node and to the process/stage it is most relevant to, consistent with how other governance artifacts are tagged (Section 4.6, FR-DA-GOV-08).

The system shall index every saved REX entry into the same retrieval corpus used for AI Use Case grounding, the AI Assistant, and application-help search (Section 4.5), scoped to the requesting user’s own tenant, so a relevant prior REX entry can surface in a future suggestion or answer.

The system shall provide a REX Register view aggregating entries by category/tag and by rating, so a recurring root cause or a declining rating trend is visible without reading every entry individually.
The system shall version every REX entry via the generic Version Management service (Section 3.8/4.16), retaining its full edit history and supporting revert to any prior version.

The system shall gate REX entry management behind a dedicated capability, and shall scope every REX read and every retrieval-grounded reference to it to the requesting user’s own tenant, consistent with the platform’s multi-tenancy requirement (Section 4.1).

The system shall present the REX prompt to the user who performed the closing action, immediately after the closure succeeds, with a choice to fill it in now or skip; skipping shall leave the closure intact and the entry available to add later from the REX Register.

The system shall generate the primary menu from a single navigation model in which each item declares its module group, label, icon, route, and the view permission and Solution Pack entitlement it requires, and shall show only the items the current user can open.
The system shall group menu items by module, let the user collapse and expand each group, and mark the current screen as the active item.

The system shall let each user pin the menu open or unpin it. Unpinned, the menu shall collapse to an edge handle, slide over the content when the user points at the edge, focuses the handle, or uses the menu button, and slide away again when the pointer leaves or an item is chosen.

The system shall let each user dock the menu on the left, right, top, or bottom edge of the screen, laying it out vertically on the left and right and horizontally, with drop-down groups, on the top and bottom.
The system shall let each user mark menu items as favorites, shown in a Favorites group at the start of the menu.

The system shall store the dock position, pinned state, collapsed groups, and favorites as server-side user preferences, applied on every sign-in and on any device, and shall offer them both from the menu itself and from the user's Settings screen.
The system shall treat left and right as logical start and end under right-to-left languages, mirroring the dock position and the slide direction when Arabic is selected.

The system shall, below a mobile breakpoint, replace the docked menu with a drawer opened from a menu button and closed by Escape, by an outside tap, or by choosing an item, without changing the user's stored desktop preferences.

The system shall make the shell fully keyboard-operable: a skip-to-content link as the first focusable element, menu and group buttons exposing their expanded state, Escape closing any open menu, and the active item marked as the current page for assistive technologies.
The system shall keep the Organization/Project context switcher, language switcher, notification indicator, AI Assistant entry point, and user menu in the header bar of every authenticated screen.

The system shall organize the menu by what users do, in a documented order (home and own work, portfolio of records, process design, governance and risk, AI and knowledge, reports, administration, personal settings), so the same capability is always found in the same place across Dynamic Apps.

The system shall define its benchmark metrics in one catalog module, each with a label, a unit, a direction of good, a plain-language explanation, and a computation from the platform's own records, consumed by every benchmarking screen.

The system shall compare, within one Organization, every catalog metric across the segments of at least one dimension the application defines (for example record or project type, process track, or owning OBS node), showing each segment's value, the Organization-wide value, and the median.

The system shall compare, across the Organizations of the requester's Group, per-Organization aggregates of the same metrics, and shall rank each Organization per metric according to the metric's direction of good, giving tied values the same rank.

The system shall include in a Group comparison only per-metric aggregates and each contributing Organization's name and sector — never a record, record title, person's name, or identifier from another Organization.
The system shall flag any segment or Organization with fewer records than a minimum sample size (default 3) as not comparable, and shall exclude it from ranks and medians.

The system shall let an Organization Administrator withdraw the Organization from Group benchmarking and rejoin it; while withdrawn, its figures shall not be shown to the other Organizations of the Group. Every change shall be written to the audit log.
The system shall gate internal benchmarking behind a view capability, Group comparison behind a separate capability, and the sharing setting behind a management capability, each enforced server-side.

The system shall refuse any comparison with an Organization outside the requester's Group and shall not import or display external or third-party benchmark data; an Organization with no Group shall see its internal comparison only, with a notice explaining why.

The system shall render each metric comparison as a chart following the common visual identity, with the requester's own Organization or the selected segment highlighted, and shall let the user filter the comparison by the application's segment dimensions.

The system shall take a consistent backup of its data store on demand — from the command line and from the platform administrator's configuration screen — and automatically once a day, while remaining online.
The system shall keep backups for a configurable retention period (default 14 days), delete older ones automatically, and list existing backups with date and size to the platform administrator only.
The system shall document how to restore a backup, and a restored backup from an earlier release shall start without any manual migration step (FR-DA-OPS-04).

The system shall apply additive schema and permission-catalog migrations automatically on startup, never dropping or rewriting existing data or administrator changes, so an existing installation upgrades in place.

The system shall check, when installed and started, the runtime version, port availability, and whether the data store has been initialized, and shall report each problem as a plain-language message naming the corrective action rather than a stack trace.
The system shall expose an unauthenticated health endpoint reporting only liveness, whether the data store is initialized, and the deployment mode — never tenant data.

The system shall ship a deterministic demonstration seed, reset by one command, containing at least one Group of two or more Organizations, at least one Independent Organization, several sectors, a user for every role, and at least ten instances of each principal end-to-end process per Organization, all fictional (Section 2.7).

The system shall include an administrator traceability view mapping each requirement ID of this standard to its implementation status (Met, Partial, Not met, or Deployment responsibility) and a short evidence note.

The system shall seed demonstration data in every module, so that no screen of the delivered application is empty: record teams with roles, templates, attachments in several formats, custom AI Use Cases and project overrides, alert settings and alerts already read, and integration and webhook registrations.
The system shall let the user choose a scope: a Group, one or more Organizations, or a set of principal records, each list containing only what the user may see (FR-DA-TEN-15).

The system shall show one row per principal record and one column per process stage, with at each intersection the status of that stage for that record, drawn from one status vocabulary (for example Completed, In progress, At gate, On hold, Stopped, Not started, Not in the record's variant).
The system shall show a legend of the cell statuses, a per-stage total, the number of times a stage ran when more than once, and a hover text naming record, stage and status.
The system shall export the matrix to CSV (FR-DA-REP-04) and shall show records of another Organization read-only.

The system shall keep a Checklist Library with full Create, Read, Update, Delete and Duplicate on checklist templates, each with ordered items marked mandatory and evidence-required, classified by scope (universal or one vertical) and optionally by mode and track, and versioned under the generic Version Management service (Section 3.8). A checklist shall not require a gate.

The system shall let a checklist template be related to zero, one or several gates; the association is made from the gate (FR-DA-GTE-02) or from the checklist, and a checklist associated with a gate shall be copied into that gate's checklist when the phase opens. A built-in reference checklist shall apply to a gate that has no associated checklist.

The system shall let an authorized user add items to an open gate or phase checklist from any template or by typing them, never adding the same item twice, and save such a checklist as a new template.

The system shall show for every checklist the gates it is associated with, and let the library be filtered by gate, by "not related to a gate", by vertical, mode and track; it shall seed sector checklists for new Organizations of that sector.
The system shall freeze a checklist, its items and their evidence once the gate it belongs to has been submitted for decision or, for a checklist not related to a gate, once it has been signed off.

The system shall let a checklist that is not related to any gate be attached directly to a phase, a task or a project, with its completion tracked and reported; such a checklist shall not block any progression.

The system shall show, before a checklist is changed or deleted, the gates, templates and open phases that use it; a checklist associated with a published gate shall be retired rather than deleted, and deleting a checklist shall never alter the copies already made in projects.
The system shall let a user attach several files at once to an action or a checklist item, by file picker or drag-and-drop.

The system shall accept a published list of formats — documents, spreadsheets, presentations, images, drawings and CAD, data and models, archives, audio and video, e-mails — with a size and count limit per upload, and shall refuse any other type with a message naming the refused file.
The system shall show for every attachment its type, size, author and date, with download for every viewer and removal for its author or a manager, audited, and never once the stage is submitted.
The system shall store attachments outside every web-served directory, scoped to the tenant, and include them in the backup instructions (NFR-DA-SEC-13, FR-DA-OPS-01).

The system shall support the definition of verticals, each with a unique identifier, a short prefix, a name, a description, its target segments, its value proposition, and its associated macro and E2E processes.
The system shall support a taxonomy of verticals with parent-child and sibling relationships.
The system shall let administrators and partners define new verticals without modifying the platform, and new verticals shall work alongside existing ones.

The system shall manage each vertical through the lifecycle Draft, Review, Approved, Active, Deprecated and Retired, with an approval workflow (configurable approvers, escalation and notifications) for definition, activation, modification, deprecation and retirement.

The system shall version-control vertical definitions under the Version Management service (Section 3.8), so that every change can be tracked, reviewed, approved and rolled back, including the rollback of an activation or configuration change to a previous version.
The system shall let each tenant activate its own set of verticals without affecting other tenants.

The system shall refuse to deactivate a vertical, a macro process or an E2E process while active projects depend on it, shall require approval for a deactivation, and shall preserve all data of a deactivated vertical.

The system shall keep an immutable, searchable and exportable audit trail of every vertical action — definition, activation, modification, deactivation and retirement — retained per policy (Section 4.11).
The system shall record a designated owner for every vertical and shall support change management for it: change request, impact analysis, approval and tracked implementation.
The system shall capture and report governance metrics per vertical: adoption, compliance and performance.
The system shall activate the macro processes of a vertical when the vertical is activated, with a configurable range of three to five per vertical.

The system shall describe every vertical macro process with an identifier, name, description, goals, input suppliers, inputs, tasks, outputs, output customers, related E2E processes, related modules and applicable compliance requirements.
The system shall map each vertical macro process to the regulatory and industry standards that apply to it; the mapping shall be configurable and audited.
The system shall let administrators and partners add vertical macro processes without modifying the platform, versioned and reversible like verticals (FR-DA-VRT-05).

The system shall support tasks within each macro process (owner, deadline, dependencies, status) and steps within each task (owner, inputs, outputs, status), and shall enforce the dependencies defined between macro processes, tasks and steps.
The system shall activate the E2E processes of a vertical when the vertical is activated, with a configurable range of two to four per vertical.

The system shall enforce the chain relationships between E2E processes — sequential, branching, parallel, loop-back and terminal — and shall support, per E2E process, triggers (business event, time-based, manual) and terminal states (success, failure, cancellation, loop-back).
The system shall support user-facing tasks in each E2E process, each linked to the macro processes, tasks and steps it relies on.

The system shall capture metrics for each vertical macro and E2E process — cycle time, completion rate, quality and compliance — and produce status, compliance and performance reports from them (Section 4.8).

The system shall let a vertical extend the common data model with its own objects, attributes, relationships, validation rules and lifecycle states, without altering or breaking the common entities (Section 6).
The system shall exchange vertical data in industry-standard formats, at least JSON, XML, CSV and PDF, and, where the vertical needs it, engineering formats such as STEP, IGES and JT.
The system shall apply per-vertical retention policies and support archiving and retrieval of vertical data, in line with the regulatory retention of the sector.
The system shall support vertical-specific regulations and standards as configurable, audited and reportable compliance requirements, subject to FR-DA-CFG-09.

The system shall monitor compliance per vertical, alert stakeholders of non-compliance through the Notification Center (Section 4.9), and produce compliance reports, audit reports and certification records.

The system shall support internal and external compliance audits — planning, execution, findings and corrective actions — and vertical compliance training with content, delivery, tracking and certification.
The system shall connect vertical-specific external systems through standard interfaces (REST, SOAP, GraphQL, file-based, message-based), under the integration rules of FR-DA-CFG-10 to 14.
The system shall secure, monitor (performance, errors, data quality) and test every vertical integration, and shall handle integration errors by retry, fallback and notification.
The system shall let an administrator configure, per vertical: macro and E2E process activation, checklist templates, gate criteria and data model extensions.
The system shall provide a pre-built configuration template per vertical for rapid deployment.
The system shall validate a vertical configuration for completeness, consistency and compliance before activation, and shall refuse an activation that fails validation, naming each failed rule.
The system shall version every vertical configuration change and audit who changed what, when and why.

The system shall define an SME by configurable employee thresholds per region (default 1–250 in the EU, up to 500 under the US SBA definition) and shall segment SMEs into Micro (1–10), Small (10–50) and Medium (50–250).
The system shall let an Organization activate the SME mode together with any vertical, and each tenant shall activate its own tracks and configuration without affecting other tenants.
The system shall support two to four configurable SME tracks, each defining its number of macro processes, E2E processes, gates, checklist items per gate, and typical duration.

The system shall activate three to five SME macro processes and two to six SME E2E processes when a track is selected, with the same taxonomy, task, step, chain and metric rules as vertical processes (FR-DA-VPR-02, 05, 07, 08 and 09) plus track applicability and cost metrics.
The system shall let administrators define new SME tracks, macro processes and configurations without modifying the platform.

The system shall assign a project in SME mode to the track recommended by its complexity score (Section 4.30); a manual override shall require a written justification and an approval, and shall be audited and reportable.
The system shall capture and report, per track, its usage, effectiveness and outcomes.

The system shall govern the SME framework like verticals: a designated owner, an approval workflow for track definition, activation, modification, deprecation and retirement, change management, an immutable audit trail and adoption, compliance and performance metrics.
The system shall compute a complexity score for every project from weighted criteria and shall use it to recommend the mode and track.

The system shall let an administrator configure the criteria — at least strategic impact, technical novelty, regulatory burden, investment size, cross-functional scope, market uncertainty and time-to-market pressure — and their weights, which shall sum to 100 %; a set of weights that does not sum to 100 % shall be refused.

The system shall let each vertical add its own complexity drivers (for example regulatory burden, industry standards, sector-specific risks) with their weights, versioned, so that the score and the recommended track reflect the vertical of the project.
The system shall keep an audit trail of every score — criteria, weights, values, result and track assignment — and shall report the distribution of scores, track assignments and outcomes.

The system shall run an onboarding plan for an SME within a configurable period (default 30 days): tenant provisioning (FR-DA-TEN-14), track configuration, data import, validation, user training and go-live.

The system shall import data from spreadsheets, CSV files, legacy systems and cloud storage, preserving data integrity and relationships, and shall validate the imported data for completeness, consistency and accuracy before go-live, listing every rejected record with its reason.
The system shall provide self-service training and guided onboarding: interactive tutorials, guided workflows, sample data and contextual help (Section 4.12).

The system shall offer SME users simplified navigation, a mobile-responsive or progressive web app experience, and self-service support through the knowledge base, the AI Assistant (Section 4.10) and a community space.
The system shall measure onboarding: time-to-value, data quality, user adoption and satisfaction.

The system shall let an administrator define three to five SME packs, each with configurable contents, target segment and price, and bundles of a vertical pack with an SME pack, each recorded as a Solution Pack variant so that entitlement stays enforced by FR-DA-CFG-06.

The system shall enforce configurable pricing rules — minimum price per user per month, minimum user count per pack, volume discounts and bundle discounts — and shall show how each price was obtained.
The system shall support upgrading and downgrading between packs and bundles with prorated billing and without loss of data.
The system shall report revenue, discounts, adoption, upgrades and downgrades per pack and bundle, exportable to PDF, XML and CSV.
The system shall keep a Project Template Catalog in which every template is classified by scope — Universal (common to all sectors) or one Vertical — and by mode — Full, or SME with its track.

The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, Delete and Duplicate on project templates, versioned under Section 3.8; a template shall carry its default fields, its phases, the gates (Section 4.35) and checklists (Section 4.23) attached to each phase, its OBS roles and its milestones.

The system shall present the catalog as a browsable list with search and filters on scope, vertical, mode, track and status, a preview of each template's phases, gates and checklists, and its use count.

The system shall manage each template through Draft, Published and Retired; only published templates shall be offered at project creation, and retiring a template shall not change any project created from it.

The system shall provide universal templates for Full and SME mode on every installation, seed vertical templates when a vertical is activated, and let an authorized user save an existing project as a new template.

The system shall restrict catalog changes to a dedicated permission, audit every change, and let platform templates be shared read-only with all Organizations while Organization templates stay private to their tenant.
The system shall offer three creation modes on one entry point: From the catalog, Manual, and With AI.

From the catalog: the system shall propose the templates that match the Organization's verticals and the project's mode and track, and copy the chosen template's fields, phases, gates, checklists and roles into the new project.

Manual: the system shall let the user enter the project and choose its vertical (or none), mode and track, and build its phases by attaching gates from the Gate Library and checklists from the Checklist Library, or by creating new ones.

With AI: the system shall draft the project — fields, complexity scores, recommended mode and track, closest template, phases, gates and checklists — from a short description, as an Assistive AI suggestion that the user accepts, modifies or rejects item by item before anything is saved (FR-DA-AI-07); the draft shall work with the built-in engine and use the live model when configured.

The system shall compute the complexity score (Section 4.30) in every creation mode, apply the quota checks of NFR-DA-SEC-08, and record in the audit trail the creation mode, the template and version used, and the AI suggestions accepted.

The system shall keep a Gate Library with full Create, Read, Update, Delete and Duplicate on gate definitions, versioned: name, purpose, entry and exit criteria, approvers (roles or people), decision options Go, No-Go, Hold and Recycle, and applicability by vertical, mode and track.

The system shall let an authorized user associate zero, one or several checklists of the Checklist Library with a gate, optionally per track, each marked mandatory or optional, in a chosen order; a checklist created from the gate screen shall be saved in the Checklist Library, and the same checklist may be associated with several gates.

The system shall let an authorized user attach one or more gates to any phase of a project or a project template, reorder them, and detach them while the phase has not started; attaching a gate brings its associated checklists with it.

The system shall configure the gates of a project from its vertical and track: the number of gates depends on the track and the criteria on the vertical, and a gate may be marked optional for a track.

The system shall block the progression of a phase while a mandatory item of a mandatory checklist associated with its gate is incomplete; enforcement shall be configurable per gate and a waiver shall require justification and approval.

The system shall capture every gate decision with its approvers, criteria results and comments, and keep an immutable audit trail of gate actions — creation, modification, checklist association, attachment to a phase, review, decision and waiver.
Changing a gate, or a checklist associated with it, shall not alter the copies already attached to started phases; the user shall be offered to update not-yet-started phases to the new version.
Dashboard and list views shall render within 2 seconds under nominal per-tenant data volumes.
An AI agent suggestion shall return within 5 seconds under its deterministic path.
A knowledge-base or FAQ retrieval search shall return ranked results within 1 second for a tenant's full corpus.
A single standard-report export (PDF, Excel, or Word) shall complete within 3 seconds for a tenant's current data volume.

With 100 concurrent users on one tenant, the 95th-percentile response time of read endpoints shall stay at or below 1 second, measured by a repeatable load test. A per-user read cache, where used, shall hold an entry for no more than 30 seconds and shall be invalidated by any write in the same Organization.
Activating a vertical, with its processes and configuration, shall complete within 5 minutes (configurable target).
A bulk data import shall load 10,000 records within 30 minutes, and an SME shall be able to complete onboarding within 30 days (configurable targets).

A production deployment offering the Vertical and SME layers shall be sized for configurable targets, by default 1,000 API calls per second sustained and 10,000 concurrent users, with reports generated within 60 seconds.
All API endpoints except login shall require a valid, signed, time-boxed authentication token.
Passwords shall be stored only as salted cryptographic hashes; plaintext passwords shall never be logged or persisted.
Every authorization decision shall be enforced server-side; client-side permission and Pack-entitlement checks are a UX convenience only, never the security boundary.
No data query shall be constructed by concatenating untrusted input; all data access shall use parameterized statements or an equivalent safe-query mechanism.
Owner/Evaluator segregation of duties, and any equivalent server-enforced business rule, shall be enforced server-side, not merely hidden in the UI.
A one-Accountable-per-RACSI-activity rule, and any equivalent uniqueness rule, shall be enforced by a data-persistence-layer constraint, not merely by disabling an option in the UI.

A Real LLM Provider Connection's API key shall be captured and stored only client-side; the backend shall never persist it to any table, write it to any log line, or return it in any API response, and any server-side proxying of a forwarded key shall use it for exactly one outbound call and never write, log, cache, or hold it beyond that request.

Every quota check (Projects, OBS nodes, AI Use Cases, and any other Pack-bound dimension) shall be enforced at the point of creation/activation on the server, never solely by disabling a client-side control; an over-quota request shall be rejected with HTTP 409, never silently truncated or partially applied.

Solution Pack entitlement shall be treated as an authorization axis independent of, and enforced in addition to, RBAC permissions; a route gated by both shall require both checks to pass, each independently testable and independently capable of producing a 403.

Individually identifiable records requiring restricted visibility (e.g. individual-level readiness or sentiment data) shall be restricted, by RBAC default, to an explicitly named set of roles; other roles shall see only aggregated, de-identified views.
Tenant data isolation shall be verified by an automated cross-tenant access test suite exercised in the build/release pipeline, not solely by code review.

The login endpoint shall be rate-limited per client, and every response shall carry standard security headers (content-type sniffing protection, frame protection, and a restrictive cross-origin resource policy).

Caches, backups, and logs shall never make one tenant's data available to another; backups shall be stored outside every web-served directory and be readable only by the service account and the platform administrator.
The system shall support standard federated authentication (SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect) and multi-factor authentication.
Role-based access control shall support scopes by vertical and by SME track in addition to the tenancy scopes.
Data shall be encrypted at rest (AES-256 or equivalent) and in transit (TLS 1.2 or later), with configurable data residency regions and optional customer-managed keys (bring your own key).

The system shall degrade gracefully if an AI agent or live-LLM call fails: the underlying CRUD operation shall still succeed, with the AI suggestion simply unavailable or served from its deterministic fallback.
The system shall target 99.9% uptime in a production deployment.
A report-export failure shall return a structured error without corrupting or partially writing the underlying report data view.
The persistence layer shall support scheduled backup with a defined retention policy; a production deployment shall not rely on a single unreplicated data file as its sole durability boundary.
The backup schedule shall bound data loss to at most 24 hours, and restoring a backup shall be tested at least once per release.

A production deployment offering the Vertical and SME layers shall support disaster recovery with an RTO under 4 hours and an RPO under 1 hour, automatic failover and automated backups, tightening NFR-DA-REL-05 for that deployment.
The architecture shall support horizontal scaling of the web tier independently of the API tier.
The system shall support at least 100 concurrent users per tenant without functional degradation.
The persistence schema and the retrieval index shall each be swappable for a distributed equivalent (e.g. a managed relational database, a vector database) without changing the API contract.

The system shall scale to configurable limits, by default 1,000 tenants per deployment including 10,000 SME tenants in shared mode, 100 million records, 500 macro processes, 200 E2E processes and 100 checklist items per gate.
Adding a vertical, an SME track, a template, a gate or a checklist shall require no downtime.
The UI, and every generated document, shall follow the suite's common visual identity (color palette, typography, iconography) consistently across all modules and output formats.
The UI shall be responsive and usable on desktop, tablet, and mobile viewport widths, with touch-target sizing meeting WCAG 2.1 AA on mobile.
All interactive controls shall be keyboard-navigable and carry accessible labels (WCAG 2.1 AA target).
Status, severity, and classification fields shall use one consistent color/badge vocabulary across every module, so a user who has learned a meaning in one module recognizes it in every other.
Every interactive target shall measure at least 24 × 24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8), and at least 44 × 44 CSS pixels on touch screens.

Every release shall pass an automated accessibility scan (e.g. axe-core) of its main screens with no critical or serious violation. Text shall meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text); where a brand color falls short, its darker tone shall be used for text, and any remaining brand conflict shall be recorded in Appendix A.

Every confirmation, warning, and error message shown as a transient notification shall be translated (FR-DA-I18N-07), announced to assistive technologies through a polite live region, and remain readable long enough to act on.
Wide matrices and tables shall scroll inside their own container, keeping the first column visible, so the page never scrolls horizontally on a 390-pixel viewport.
SME users shall complete onboarding within 1 day and need less than 4 hours of training, helped by guided workflows (configurable targets).
User satisfaction shall be measured, with a configurable target (default NPS of 30 or more).
Every layout — navigation, tables, and charts — shall render correctly mirrored under Arabic RTL, not just with mirrored text direction.
The system shall support configurable languages (default English, French, Arabic, Spanish, German), currencies (default USD, EUR, MAD, ZAR) and regional date, time and number formats.

Installation shall succeed on a fresh target machine with only a supported Node.js runtime installed — no native C/C++ build toolchain, no required external database server, and no mandatory external API key.
The same source shall run unmodified across supported operating systems via standard package-manager install/build/start commands.

Every change shall be built by a continuous-integration pipeline on Linux, Windows, and macOS that installs dependencies, seeds the demonstration data, runs the automated tests — including the cross-tenant suite of NFR-DA-SEC-11 — and builds the web client.
Each tier shall install, seed, and start with its package manager's standard commands (install, seed, dev or start), documented in a README at the root of the delivery.

Cross-cutting engines — the Action/Task Register, the Alert & Notification Engine, the RBAC layer, the KPI/Reporting engine, and the Audit Trail Service — shall be implemented as composable modules reusable by sibling Dynamic Apps via the same API contract.
AI agent implementations shall be isolated behind a stable internal interface so a rule-based implementation can be replaced by an LLM/vector-DB-backed one without changing calling code.
The Solution Pack feature and quota matrix shall be defined in exactly one place and consumed by every enforcing route, so entitlements can never drift between routes.

The AI Use Case Library's generation service shall be the single designated server-side integration point for a live LLM call and its provider-specific credential/endpoint logic; no other module shall embed its own LLM provider client.
The alert type-to-name and type-to-stage/process mapping shall be defined in exactly one shared module, consumed by both seed data and live computation.

The Installation Guide and User Guide shall be generated from source in Word and PDF, each with an automatic table of contents, and the User Guide's step-by-step walkthroughs shall be replayed automatically against a freshly seeded instance, so the documentation cannot drift from the application.

Every User Guide walkthrough shall start from the tenancy — create or choose the Group (Yes/No), create the Organization, then the principal record(s) — and the guide shall include the decision matrix of FR-DA-HLP-04.

Verticals, SME tracks, complexity criteria, packs, project templates, gates and checklists shall be configuration data loaded without code changes, and the platform shall be modular with zero-downtime upgrades, monitoring, alerting and comprehensive logging.
The application shall target evergreen desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers; no legacy-browser support is in scope.

BPMN diagrams shall be stored and exchanged as schema-valid BPMN 2.0 XML, verified by a round-trip import/export, so a diagram authored in one Dynamic App opens without error in any other BPMN 2.0-compliant tool, and vice versa.

The application's core workflows (record CRUD, approvals, alerts) shall remain fully usable on a mobile viewport without requiring a separate native application; a native or installable Progressive Web App wrapper, where offered, shall consume the same REST API (Section 7.2) with no mobile-specific endpoint variant.
Every AI-generated suggestion shall be logged with a confidence indicator and be attributable to a specific agent/use case and record, or, for the AI Assistant, to the requesting user and question.
The Controls module shall support demonstrating COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework coverage across all five components.
The system shall retain the full version history of every AI Use Case and every template indefinitely (no hard deletion of prior versions on edit or revert).

The system shall never represent, in any UI text, Help content, FAQ answer, or generated document, that activating a Compliance & Security Standard constitutes a certification, an external audit, or a legal attestation of compliance.

The system shall let verticals map to sector standards — for example IATF 16949 (automotive), AS9100 (aerospace), EU MDR and ISO 13485 (medical devices), FDA 21 CFR Part 11 (pharmaceutical), HACCP (food safety) — as scaffolds subject to FR-DA-CFG-09; certification (ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, GDPR) is an attribute of a deployment, not of the software.

Every requirement of a Dynamic App shall be traceable to its business requirement, user story, test case, release and, where applicable, customer commitment, in line with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148; requirement changes shall be classified Minor, Moderate, Major or Breaking with the matching approval and regression scope.

By default, and whenever no Real LLM Provider Connection is configured, the system shall not transmit tenant data to any third-party service; every AI capability shall run entirely within the deployment's own infrastructure using rule-based/statistical methods and RAG grounding. Only an explicitly user-configured, client-stored Real LLM Provider Connection may cause a single generation request to be sent to that user-selected third-party provider — opt-in per user, never enabled by default, and never applied to a permission-scoped data-query mode.
The system shall support both shared-infrastructure (SaaS) and dedicated/sovereign deployment options per Organization, without changing the tenant-isolation guarantee.

The system shall let an Organization Administrator configure an Organization-level live model — provider (standard providers or a custom endpoint compatible with a common API), model, temperature and maximum answer length — as an alternative to the personal connection of FR-DA-AI-08; its key shall be stored encrypted under NFR-DA-SEC-17, shown masked, and never returned in full.
